title.rendered: Sutton stars as MN’s ‘Racer’s Racer of the Year’

excerpt.rendered: Motorsport News has conducted an exclusive poll of the top...

content.rendered:
Motorsport News has conducted an exclusive poll of the top ten finishers in the 2026 British Touring Car Championship to unearth the ‘Racer’s Racer of the Year’.

Unsurprisingly, record-breaking champion Ash Sutton topped the rankings from his peers in his NAPA UK Ford Focus Titanium, whilst the likes of Team VERTU’s Tom Ingram and CPRL’s Mercedes racer Adam Morgan also finished highly.

Others to feature in the top ten include Team VERTU Hyundai racer Nic Hamilton and Jack Sears Trophy winner Dexter Patterson in his Power Maxed Racing Audi A3, but to see the full rundown you’ll have to purchase this week’s Motorsport News.

Matt James, Motorsport News editor and BTCC reporter, said: “This is me dipping my responsibility to rate the drivers in print, but who better to ask than those strapped into the cockpit themselves? It is a really strong insight into the drivers who earn respect from their on-track rivals.

“Conducting this poll gives readers an insight into who the men on the grid think are those performing excellently. And the drivers themselves don’t generally tend to get things wrong.”

The results gave NAPA Racing UK an early 33-point advantage over LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing (PMR), whose Audi squad enjoyed a strong start thanks to Mikey Doble's opening race victory and consistent results from Aiden Moffat.

title.rendered: Donington Park to host 2027 BTCC Season Launch

excerpt.rendered: Snetterton and Croft confirmed for official pre-season testing TOCA –...

content.rendered:
Snetterton and Croft confirmed for official pre-season testing

TOCA – series organiser of the British Touring Car Championship – has confirmed its pre-season test dates and official Season Launch ahead of the 2027 campaign.

The first official pre-season action will get underway at Snetterton on 9/10 March, with the Norfolk circuit hosting a two-day test as teams and drivers begin preparations for the new season.

Attention will then turn to Croft Circuit in North Yorkshire, which will stage two further days of official testing on 18/19 March.

The annual Season Launch will take place at Donington Park on 31 March, bringing the championship's teams and drivers together ahead of another eagerly anticipated season.

Drivers and teams will participate in official pre-season media activities and interviews with ITV Sport, the BTCC Media Team and other championship partners at Donington Park on 30 March, although this day will be closed to the public.

The Leicestershire venue will also host the opening rounds of the 2027 campaign on 10/11 April, with the championship returning to the National circuit just ten days after the Season Launch.

The three pre-season events will provide a sustained build-up to the new campaign, with official BTCC activity beginning in early March and continuing towards the opening race weekend in April.

Further information regarding the Season Launch programme, spectator access and activities at each venue will be announced in due course.

Please monitor the official BTCC, Snetterton, Croft and Donington Park social media channels for additional information as each event approaches.

title.rendered: Success at Mallory Park for PM Junior Championship

excerpt.rendered: The PM Junior Championship took another significant step towards its...

content.rendered:
The PM Junior Championship took another significant step towards its inaugural 2027 season with a successful Taster Day at Mallory Park, where 17 aspiring young drivers experienced the PM1 car first-hand.

Drivers from a range of backgrounds, including karting, sim racing and other junior motorsport categories, came together to try the car and discover what the new championship has to offer.

The morning sessions took place in predominantly dry conditions before rain arrived around lunchtime, leaving the circuit wet for the afternoon drivers.

The changing conditions did little to dampen the excitement. Feedback on the PM1 was consistently positive, offering further encouragement as preparations continue for the championship's first season.

Building the Next Generation

Developed by Power Maxed Racing, the PM Junior Championship offers a structured pathway for drivers aged 14–17, helping them progress from their early experiences in motorsport towards professional car racing.

At its heart is the PM1, a racing car designed to give young drivers a competitive platform to develop their skills, gain valuable experience and prepare for future opportunities in the sport.

Combining competitive racing with a strong emphasis on driver development, the championship brings together technical expertise, professional motorsport experience and opportunities for progression. It is built around three core pillars: Develop. Race. Progress.

Interest is also growing across the wider motorsport industry, with established organisations exploring the opportunities presented by the new series. This engagement highlights the PM Junior Championship's potential to become an important part of the pathway for future racing talent.

Looking Ahead to 2027

The Mallory Park Taster Day marks another milestone in the championship's preparations, giving prospective competitors a first-hand experience of the PM1 and a clearer understanding of the series ahead of its debut season.

As interest builds among drivers and the wider motorsport industry, Power Maxed Racing is working to establish a competitive, development-focused environment for the next generation of racing drivers.

The ambition goes beyond launching a new championship. By combining quality racing with opportunities to learn, develop and progress, the PM Junior Championship aims to help young competitors take the next steps in their motorsport careers.

Further details about the PM Junior Championship, driver opportunities and the 2027 season will be announced through the championship's official channels.

Tickets for the 2027 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship event at Croft are now available, with the North Yorkshire circuit launching a special offer to celebrate 30 years since the championship returned to the venue.

To mark the anniversary, the first 97 adult Sunday tickets will be available for just £30, recognising the BTCC's return to Croft in 1997. Ticket prices for the 14/15 August event have also been frozen at 2026 levels until the New Year, giving fans the opportunity to secure their places at this year's prices.

Fellow British Automobile Racing Club (BARC) venue Thruxton has also launched ticket sales for its 2027 BTCC event, with the Hampshire circuit set to welcome the championship on 24/25 July.

Fans heading to Croft next August can look forward to three headline BTCC races across the weekend, alongside a full support race programme, including the all-new PM Junior Championship, which joins the package for all ten rounds next season.

Croft and Thruxton join the growing list of venues already selling tickets for the 2027 campaign, with Motorsport Vision (MSV) circuits and Knockhill having previously launched their respective early bird offers.

Award-winning automotive retailer Vertu has extended its partnership with title-winning BTCC team EXCELR8 through to the end of the 2029 season, underlining its long-term commitment to one of the most successful teams in recent series history.

Vertu, which recently retained the title of Retailer of the Year at the Autotrader Retailer Awards, has worked with the Droitwich-based team since 2021, and took up the role of title sponsor twelve months later.

A stunning campaign saw the team secure the 2022 title thanks to Tom Ingram, and it then emerged on top in Britain’s premier racing series again in 2025.

Ingram lifted the Drivers' Championship for a second time, whilst Team VERTU completed a title treble by securing both the Teams' Championship and the Manufacturers'/Constructors' Championship.

Ahead of the 2027 season, the current agreement between Vertu and EXCELR8 has been further extended until at least the conclusion of the 2029 campaign, cementing the partnership as one of the longest-running and most successful commercial relationships in the BTCC paddock.

Team VERTU will continue to field a four-car programme in the BTCC next season and has already confirmed the signing of teenage racer Noah Young to compete alongside Ingram, who will be looking to reclaim the title having finished the 2026 season as runner-up.

The remaining two drivers in the line-up will be confirmed in due course ahead of the campaign getting underway at Donington Park in April.

Justina Williams, EXCELR8 Team Owner, said: "We’re hugely proud of the strength of our relationship with Vertu, and to be able to confirm an extension to cover the next three seasons in the BTCC.

"Vertu has played a major role in the success we've enjoyed in recent years, helping us build a championship-winning programme that has delivered race victories, multiple titles and consistent on-track success.

“The security of knowing we can count on Vertu’s support through to at least the end of 2029 allows us to focus on long-term planning, and we’re looking forward to challenging for more titles alongside Vertu in the years to come.”

Robert Forrester, Chief Executive of Vertu, said: “Our partnership with EXCELR8 has delivered outstanding results both on and off the track, and has been a platform for building awareness of the Vertu brand whilst also allowing us to engage with audiences throughout the UK

"Since first joining forces with the team, we have enjoyed championship success, significant increases in brand awareness and countless opportunities to showcase the strength of the Vertu brand to millions of motorsport followers.

"This partnership works so well because of the shared drive and desire to constantly improve in order to maintain the highest levels of performance and remain at the very top.

"Extending our commitment through to the end of 2029 will allow us to build on everything we have achieved together so far, and we look forward to challenging for more success in the seasons ahead."

content.rendered:
Speedworks Corolla Racing brought the curtain down on the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship in impressive fashion at Brands Hatch, with two podium finishes for Josh Cook and another hugely encouraging weekend for Ryan Bensley.

Competing on the iconic Grand Prix circuit, the Cheshire-based outfit demonstrated the pace and potential of its Toyota Corolla GR Sport throughout the season finale, with Cook firmly amongst the frontrunners from the outset and Bensley continuing his rapid progression in Britain's premier domestic motorsport championship.

Sunday's opening encounter, Round 28 of the championship, delivered an impressive performance from Cook. Immediately involved in the battle for victory, the #66 demonstrated excellent racecraft on his way to second place.

Cook also recorded the fastest lap of the race, providing further evidence of the Corolla's outright competitiveness and securing another podium finish.

Further down the order, Bensley produced one of his most encouraging performances of the season to make up four places in the opening encounter.

Round 29 brought another opportunity for Cook to challenge at the front, and once again he delivered, securing his second runner-up finish of the afternoon and completing an impressive sequence of three consecutive top-three finishes across the Qualifying Race and Sunday's opening two encounters.

The final race of the season, Round 30, featured the traditional reverse-grid draw, with Cook selected to start eighth.

Running on the soft-compound tyre, Cook produced another measured and determined drive, working his way forward to sixth position at the chequered flag to complete a highly successful final weekend.

For Bensley, the championship finale provided a fitting conclusion to his first partial BTCC campaign. Producing another competitive drive and continuing to make progress through the field, he crossed the line in 14th position.

Josh Cook, #66, Speedworks Corolla Racing: "It was a really positive weekend and a great way to round off the championship. The car felt strong pretty much from the moment we rolled out, and that gave us the confidence to really attack.

"Qualifying was incredibly close. We topped our group and ultimately missed pole by just a couple of hundredths, which was frustrating, but it showed we had the pace to fight right at the front.

"The qualifying race was a good battle, and then on Sunday we were able to take another two podiums. Getting the fastest lap in Race One was particularly satisfying.

"Naturally, you always want to win, and when you're that close to the front you can't help feeling there was perhaps a little bit more available. But two second places, three podiums across the weekend and fourth in the championship was a strong way to finish.

"It was a season of highs and lows, and there were occasions where we had the speed without quite getting the reward. But the team never stopped pushing, and I can't thank everyone enough for the effort they've put in.

"There's a huge amount of potential in this package, and hopefully we've given everyone a good reminder of what we're capable of."

Ryan Bensley, #7, Speedworks Corolla Racing: "I absolutely loved that weekend. Brands Hatch GP is an incredible circuit, but it's also a massive challenge, particularly when you're still relatively new to touring cars.

"Qualifying wasn't quite where I wanted it to be, and that's definitely something I need to keep working on. It's about getting everything together over one lap, building confidence quickly and knowing exactly where the limits are.

"But the races were a completely different story. I felt like I was making progress every time I went out, and the pace we had, particularly on Sunday, was really encouraging.

"In Race One we went from 21st to 17th, and to be setting lap times comparable to cars much further up the field was a massive confidence boost. Then to finish the final race in 14th was a really positive way to end the year.

"I've learned an unbelievable amount since joining Speedworks. The level of engineering, preparation and support is incredible, and having someone like Josh alongside me has been invaluable.

"I know there's still a lot for me to learn, but I feel like I'm making some really big steps forward now. I'm already excited about what we can achieve in 2027, and I can't wait to keep building on everything we've learned this year."

LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing's Mikey Doble enjoyed a sensational start to the 2026 campaign, claiming victory in the opening encounter around the 1.98-mile Donington Park National circuit to give the new Audi A3 Saloon a winning debut.

The Surrey-based racer arrived at the Leicestershire venue following an encouraging pre-season testing programme, with the newly developed machinery showing promising pace ahead of its first competitive appearance.

However, the result would change following post-race checks, with Ingram disqualified for a significant overboost infringement, promoting Doble to victory and delivering an incredible first race win for the new Audi.

The result marked Doble's second career BTCC victory, following his maiden success at Snetterton in 2025, whilst also giving Power Maxed Racing the perfect start to its new chapter with the Audi.

Reflecting on the achievement, Doble said: "To take a win straight out of the box is phenomenal."

That opening triumph would prove to be the first of two outright race victories for Doble during the campaign, with the 27-year-old returning to the top step of the podium at Croft in September to take his career tally to three.

Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing's Dexter Patterson rounded off his 2026 campaign in style, securing a career-best third-place finish in the final race of the season around the 2.43-mile Brands Hatch Grand Prix circuit.

Patterson maintained his position amongst the frontrunners throughout the 18-lap encounter, eventually taking the chequered flag in fourth.

However, a five-second post-race penalty for Collard following a Safety Car restart infringement promoted Cammish to victory, Sutton to second and Patterson to third, securing the Scotsman's first-ever overall BTCC podium.

The result marked a significant milestone for the Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing driver, who had previously enjoyed success in the Jack Sears Trophy but had yet to stand on the outright BTCC rostrum.

The celebrations didn't end there, as Patterson went on to lift the 2026 Jack Sears Trophy, having secured the title at the penultimate event of the campaign.

It was also a memorable weekend for the wider Power Maxed Racing operation, with Patterson raising one of three championship trophies that the Audi racing squad took home.

A maiden overall podium, a first BTCC championship title and a memorable end to the season ensured Patterson's Brands Hatch finale earned him a nomination for the 2026 Fans' Choice Award.

title.rendered: Manufacturers'/Constructors' Championship runner-up caps impressive debut for CPRL

excerpt.rendered: CPRL wrapped up its maiden Kwik Fit British Touring Car...

content.rendered:
CPRL wrapped up its maiden Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship campaign with an impressive second-place finish in the Manufacturers'/Constructors' standings. Its Mercedes-AMG A35 saloons notched 676 points, including nine podium finishes and a fifth-place finish in the Drivers’ Championship for Adam Morgan.

Morgan took to the famed 'GP Circuit' in Group 1 in qualifying, finishing with the seventh-quickest time, while in Group 2 Dan Rowbottom was sixth, leaving the pair starting the Qualifying Race from 11th and 14th, respectively.

Rowbottom started well, gaining three places and eventually finishing seventh, while Morgan had turbo wastegate issues, fell down the order, and took the flag in 18th.

The Lancastrian responded well during the first of Sunday’s three 15-lap races, gaining five places early on and another four as he battled his way into ninth, though he was subsequently given a time penalty for contact, dropping him to 11th. It was a tougher one for Rowbottom, who fell back early on and had to consolidate his position in 12th.

The penultimate race was a quieter affair, with Morgan gaining a place early on, but as he tried to gain another position, he was found wide at Paddock Hill Bend and lost momentum, dropping back two places to once again finish 11th. Behind, Rowbottom fell back at the start and was unable to fight back, taking the flag 14th.

Opting for different setups for the final race of the 2026 season, both drivers started well and appeared to have avoided trouble at turn one. However, the #32's race unravelled moments later when a car ahead lost control and spun across his path, leaving him with nowhere to go.

Rowbottom did well to recover from the gravel and continue, but was ultimately forced to retire. Pulling to the side of the circuit, damage sustained to a brake duct in the earlier contact caused the brakes to overheat, resulting in a small fire that was quickly brought under control.

Morgan, however, had gained two positions early on and, after a lengthy Safety Car to clean things up, went on the charge all the way to fifth position. After another Safety Car period to recover his teammate's Mercedes, the #33 slipped back a place but was classified in fifth after post-race penalties were handed out, helping the team to finish second in the Manufacturers'/Constructors' standings in a superb maiden campaign.

Following its memorable debut season, CPRL will continue working to further develop the race-winning Mercedes-AMG A35 saloons as it prepares for a planned return to the BTCC in 2027.

Adam Morgan, #33, said: “It's great to have finished fifth in the championship. The changes we made for the final race definitely paid off. We still haven't quite found the ideal balance with the car, but we have a good understanding of what the issue is.

“More than anything, I have to say a massive thank you to everybody at CPRL. They worked tirelessly throughout the winter and all the way through the season. Everyone has put in a huge amount of effort, and for me to achieve my best-ever championship result with a brand-new car is something I'm incredibly proud of. The fact we've been able to achieve that while still learning and developing the package shows just how much potential there is.”

Dan Rowbottom, #32, said: “Finishing second in the Manufacturers’ standings is a testament to how hard everyone has worked, and I think it's what we deserved in the end. If the championship was based purely on effort, we'd have won it comfortably given everything we've had to overcome this year.

“It was quite an emotional day. I always find race three at the final event a bit emotional because you never know whether you'll get another season like this. I wanted to thank all the boys over the radio at the end, but sadly I didn't get the chance. The whole team has put an incredible amount into the programme and I'm proud of what we've achieved.”

title.rendered: Taylor-Smith’s Wet Weather Win: A Decade in the Making

excerpt.rendered: The 2026 TOCA Night of Champions at Silverstone in November...

content.rendered:
The 2026 TOCA Night of Champions at Silverstone in November will celebrate the standout moments from this year's Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, with the Fans' Choice Award once again giving you the opportunity to decide which achievement deserves recognition.

This year, five unforgettable moments are in contention, from emotional triumphs and long-awaited victories to breakthrough podiums and landmark wins. Today, we're looking back at Árón Taylor-Smith's remarkable wet-weather drive from 13th to victory at Brands Hatch, ending a ten-year wait for BTCC success.

Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Árón Taylor-Smith produced one of the standout performances of the 2026 campaign, charging through the field in treacherous conditions around the 1.2-mile Brands Hatch Indy circuit to claim his first BTCC victory since Rockingham in 2016.

The Irishman lined up 13th on the grid for the second encounter of the weekend, with damp conditions greeting the field before the rain began to fall heavier as the race progressed.

The vast majority of drivers elected to remain on slick Goodyear tyres, setting the stage for a fascinating battle as grip levels continued to deteriorate around the Kent circuit.

NAPA Racing UK's Ash Sutton and Team VERTU's Ricky Collard both enjoyed spells at the front of the field, but it was the charging Taylor-Smith who was rapidly making his way through the order.

The #50 Toyota Corolla GR Sport looked particularly comfortable in the challenging conditions, with Taylor-Smith picking off his rivals as others struggled to maintain their pace on the increasingly slippery surface.

Having started outside the top ten, the experienced Irishman soon found himself challenging for the lead, eventually diving down the inside of Collard's Hyundai i30 N at Paddock Hill Bend to complete his charge from P13 to P1.

Once out front, Taylor-Smith continued to stretch his advantage over the chasing pack, eventually crossing the line 3.409 seconds clear of Sutton, with Collard completing the podium positions.

The victory marked a significant milestone for both driver and team, with Taylor-Smith returning to the top step of the BTCC podium for the first time in almost a decade, whilst Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport celebrated its first victory since beginning its new chapter as a two-car operation.

Having last tasted outright success at Rockingham in 2016, the Dubliner's Brands Hatch triumph brought an end to a lengthy wait for his fifth career BTCC victory.

Reflecting on the achievement, Taylor-Smith said: "Today feels so surreal, it's like a dream. We've been working so hard as a team to unlock a bit more performance from this Corolla, and to have the best reward today with a victory is honestly the greatest feeling for everyone involved."

The #50 driver also credited a small adjustment to his Toyota between races with transforming its performance, allowing him to make the most of the difficult conditions.

A remarkable drive through the field, a first victory in ten years and a memorable moment for Taylor-Smith and Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport, earning the Irishman a nomination for the 2026 Fans' Choice Award.

title.rendered: Team VERTU signs off 2026 BTCC campaign with double victory

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU signed off for the 2026 Kwik Fit British...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU signed off for the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season with a double win at Brands Hatch, and it could have been more following at the final race of the campaign.

Tom Ingram made a strong start to the opening race on Sunday morning to hit the front of the field ahead of Aiden Moffat before the Audi driver managed to reclaim the lead when he dived down the inside on the GP loop. 

However, Ingram refused to let his rival break away and despite having less TOCA Turbo Boost at his disposal, made a move around the outside at Clearways to reclaim a lead he would retain to the finish.

Moving up into fourth on the opening lap, Ricky Collard held position throughout the race to finish just off the podium on the road, but a penalty for Moffat would see him promoted into third spot to give the team a double podium finish.

Tom Chilton climbed to 13th place before he was handed a time penalty that dropped him a spot in the results, with Hamilton rounding out the finishers in 20th place.

From pole for the second race of the weekend, Ingram controlled proceedings from the front to make it two wins from two, although Collard was unable to replicate his earlier result as he faded to seventh having been overhauled by a number of drivers running the soft compound tyre.

Chilton would find himself embroiled in a huge battle I’m the midfield pack before being classified in twelfth, with Hamilton dicing with Ryan Bensley and Nick Halstead throughout before finishing in 21st.

The final race of the season would start in disappointing fashion as both Ingram and Chilton were forced out after an incident going into turn one, leaving Collard to fly the flag for Team VERTU as he blasted his way to the front on the opening lap from the second row of the grid.

From there, Collard was able to maintain his position at the front of the pack despite huge pressure from behind to cross the line first before a penalty for a restart infringement dropped him back to eighth place.

Hamilton meanwhile rounded out the season with 16th place to just miss out on an overall points finish.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“The weekend hasn’t gone the way I wanted it to in terms of the results, but I’ve felt a lot of love from everyone - from the fans, from colleagues and former colleagues, and from my family and friends. 

“It’s been a hugely emotional experience and at one point, I though the stars might align and we’d be on reverse grid pole with the soft tyres. I’m pretty confident that we could have gone for the win and achieved the dream of starting and ending my BTCC career with a trophy, but instead I signed off with a Vertu pirouette into the gravel with Tom!

“A huge thank you to everyone who has supported me through the years as I’ve had an absolute blast as a professional racing driver. Competing in the BTCC for so long has been the most amazing experience and I’m going to miss it, but I love this series and you can rest assured that I’ll still be watching on as a fan and cheering on!”

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“I can honestly say this has been one of the best weekends I’ve ever had in motorsport. Regardless of the final result, I enjoyed every single moment of it. Of course, we all race to win, but sometimes the memories, the people and the journey mean far more than any trophy ever could.

“This season has been an incredible chapter in my career. To think I wasn’t even expecting to be on the grid at the start of the year, to then come back and fight at the front with some of the best drivers in the country, is something I’m incredibly proud of.

“I also want to wish my team-mate Tom all the very best in his retirement. It’s been a privilege sharing the garage with him and being part of his final season. He’s achieved so much in this sport and deserves to enjoy whatever comes next.

“I had the biggest smile on my face all weekend, and that’s how I want to remember it. I love what I do, I love racing. I’m excited for whatever the future holds.”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“It’s been a tough weekend for me to end the season but that is what touring cars is all about. Not every weekend is going to be smooth sailing but I kept fighting until the end and we had a good race to finish things off.

“I’ve never known from year to year if I would get the sponsorship and the partners to go racing, and I am hugely privileged and honoured to be part of this grid. No-one else has to drive with a disability like I do, and it’s a massive achievement to even be out there competing.

“Moving into one of the top seats on the grid, I knew there would be people who would question me this year but I think everyone can see the progress I’ve made and how I’ve developed as a driver. This has been the best season of my touring car career by some margin and I feel I’ve proved a point with some of my performances on track.

“The highlight is obvious and getting on the podium at Snetterton is an experience that will live with me forever. It’s something I want more in the future and the hard work has already started behind the scenes to try and ensure that I can return next season to build on the foundations we have put in place this year.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“The final race wasn’t how I expected the season to finish but it almost sums up our year as something completely outside our control prevented a good weekend from being a great one! 

“Before the final race, things had been going really well and the car was absolutely mega earlier in the day. The fight with Aiden in race one is what the BTCC is all about as it was hard but fair racing that I really enjoyed and to come out on top of a battle like that was particularly pleasing, especially given the different levels of TTB we had.

“Leading race two from the front was also great and was further indication of the pace we’ve had all season but - for whatever reason - we haven’t been able to show.

“The season as whole obviously hasn’t delivered what we were looking for at the start, but I’m hugely proud of the team for the way they’ve continued to fight hard when things weren’t going our way.

“Ash deserved the championship this season as he’s had a fantastic year, but I don’t plan to let him have it all his own way in 2027.”

title.rendered: Hamilton's Magic Moment: A Snetterton Triumph to Remember

excerpt.rendered: The 2026 TOCA Night of Champions at Silverstone in November...

content.rendered:
The 2026 TOCA Night of Champions at Silverstone in November will celebrate the standout moments from this year's Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, with the Fans' Choice Award once again giving you the opportunity to decide which achievement deserves recognition.

This year, five unforgettable moments are in contention, from emotional triumphs and long-awaited victories to breakthrough podiums and landmark wins. Today, we're looking back at one of the most heartwarming occasions of the season: Nic Hamilton's maiden Jack Sears Trophy triumph at Snetterton.

Team VERTU's Nic Hamilton claimed the first silverware of his racing career following three determined performances around the 2.97-mile Norfolk circuit, sparking one of the most emotional podium celebrations in recent BTCC history.

The Hyundai i30 N driver had already opened his overall championship points account at Brands Hatch, and continued that progress during Saturday's Qualifying Race, climbing to 15th to add another point to his tally.

Sunday's opening encounter saw Hamilton recover from a difficult getaway to finish 17th overall, battling his way ahead of race winners Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) and Árón Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport).

Whilst Restart Racing's James Dorlin claimed the opening Jack Sears Trophy victory, Hamilton continued his progress in Race 2, fighting back after a slow start to take 16th overall and second in class behind NAPA Racing UK's Lewis Selby.

It was a similar story in the reverse grid finale, as the #28 once again recovered from a challenging getaway to finish 16th overall and second amongst the JST contenders, this time behind Selby's teammate Sam Osborne.

Despite not claiming an individual class victory across the three encounters, Hamilton's consistency was enough to secure the overall Jack Sears Trophy honours for the weekend, marking the first podium appearance of his BTCC career.

What followed was an unforgettable scene as an enormous crowd gathered to celebrate the achievement, with multiple champions Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport), Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU) joining fans and fellow competitors in cheering Hamilton onto the rostrum.

The trio, boasting nine BTCC Drivers' titles between them at the time, joined the celebrations as the Team VERTU driver received his trophy, with the emotion of the occasion clear throughout the paddock.

Born with cerebral palsy and having been told as a child that he would never walk, Hamilton had achieved a lifelong ambition, with the 34-year-old later admitting that he had never expected to leave Snetterton as a Jack Sears Trophy winner.

Reflecting on the occasion, Hamilton said: "I've always said that I wanted to win a trophy, but I didn't want to just be gifted it."

It was a special moment for Hamilton and the wider BTCC community, as years of hard work and determination culminated in a maiden trophy and a celebration that brought the house down at Snetterton.

excerpt.rendered: The MINI CHALLENGE will continue to form part of the...

content.rendered:
The MINI CHALLENGE will continue to form part of the biggest show in British motorsport for the next three years after agreeing an extended deal to remain on the support package for the prestigious British Touring Car Championship.

The new agreement, which takes effect at the end of the current deal, will see the highly competitive one-make series continue to fill one of the coveted BTCC support slots until at least the end of the 2029 season.

The announcement comes on the back of a dramatic season of competition in the MINI CHALLENGE’s headline JCW class, further cementing its position as one of the leading categories in UK motorsport.

Defending champion Tom Ovenden eventually retained his crown, beating rival Max Edmundson by a single point following an emotional final round on the Brands Hatch Grand Prix circuit.

As has been the case since the MINI CHALLENGE first joined the BTCC support package in 2020, the JCW class will continue to run exclusively on the TOCA package for the next three years.

JCW cars take visual cues from the current F66 MINI Cooper road car, with two-litre turbocharged engines and aggressive styling giving them the appearance of miniature touring cars.

The entry-level Cooper class, featuring cars based on the first-generation R50 MINI, will continue to run at selected events, with the 2027 calendar to be confirmed in due course.

The extended agreement between the MINI CHALLENGE and BTCC organiser TOCA also ensures the series will continue to benefit from extensive free-to-air coverage on ITV.

The broadcaster’s latest agreement with the BTCC, announced earlier this year, also runs to the end of the 2029 season.

Andy Menzies, MINI CHALLENGE Director, said:

“Following an astonishing final round for the JCW class at Brands Hatch, we are delighted to confirm a new deal that will keep us on the BTCC package for at least the next three seasons.

“Competing alongside the BTCC provides an outstanding platform for our teams, drivers and partners, as well as fantastic exposure through ITV’s free-to-air coverage.

“Extending this deal provides long-term stability for the series, our teams and drivers, allowing them to invest in their programmes and plan for the future, knowing they will continue to compete on the biggest stage in British motorsport.

“We’re proud that the MINI CHALLENGE has become such a popular part of BTCC weekends, and we look forward to building on that success over the next three years.”

Alan Gow, British Touring Car Championship Chief Executive, said:

“The MINI CHALLENGE has established itself as a popular and valuable part of the BTCC package since our relationship began back in 2020.

"The quality of our support races remains an important part of the overall BTCC experience, adding more variety and entertainment for fans at the circuit and those watching on ITV and around the world. The MINI CHALLENGE consistently delivers excellent racing, providing a perfect example of the close competition and drama that help to make our race weekends what they are.

“We look forward to continuing our relationship with the MINI CHALLENGE over at least the next three seasons.”
